parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes a traveller-facing universal exclusion: the division's statute bars restroom/changing-room use consistent with identity in every state/local government building — airports, courthouses, parks, schools, universities, jails and immigration detention — enforced by an on-site authority figure and criminal trespass on refusal, with one documented arrest (later dismissed on standing, so untested, not vindicated). The national layer supplies entry-stage exposure: no X-marker processing, refusal where sex is doubted, potential lifetime fraud ineligibility, and documented detentions of foreign nationals prompting allied advisories. Detention conditions are documented as abusive (immigration custody beatings, forced labour, sexual abuse; conversion-style prison policies) with no working remedy. Care access is squeezed and remedies are litigation-dependent and unresolved. Private businesses are outside the statute and a national hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but these do not reach the facility, border or custody exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules bar self-selected markers and X-marker processing; a 2025 cable directs refusal where sex is doubted and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; passports blocked; foreign governments issued advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; a misrepresentation finding is never automatic and requires four elements; litigation challenging the policy is pending; legal-aid guidance exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-issued marker meets national screening; a discrepancy moves the traveller from questioning to refusal, detention or an ineligibility finding, then into the custody regime.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; the corrections bureau adopted conversion-style policies (hair cut, hormones removed) and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry-stage refusal or fraud allegation feeds directly into these facilities, with no documented consular or complaint remedy changing outcomes.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division statute bars identity-congruent restrooms/changing rooms in all state/local government buildings (airports, courthouses, parks, schools, universities, prisons, immigration detention); refusal to depart is criminal trespass; one arrest, held in a men's ward; national order bars access in federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses are outside the statute; trespass requires refusal after being asked to leave; the sole prosecution was dismissed — on standing, leaving the statute untested.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local authority figures decide on site; the national order and the division statute reinforce each other, and neither yields to a foreign passport.

care_services.exposure: Division law bars insurance coverage for adult care, restricts provision to physicians, and permits conscience-based refusal; national measures target minors' care and would bar public reimbursement; an executive order frames such care as mutilation.
care_services.protection: A June 2024 court order blocked key division provisions; several national orders are enjoined; appellate status unresolved.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency or continuing care encounters conscience refusals and restricted adult provision; ward-placement practice for visitors is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: A 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises rapid neutralisation of groups described as radically pro-transgender; a justice-department reward memo invokes radical gender ideology; an order directs prosecution of teachers using preferred names.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have enjoined several orders; a national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the stakes of any police or investigative contact arising from a document or facility encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care is banned in the division and 27 states; division law allows custody modification where a child receives care; the facility statute covers all schools, private included; an order targets teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Court orders blocked the division's care provisions (status on appeal unresolved); some national orders are enjoined.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces school-facility exclusion, care denial and, at the extreme, custody consequences, with only litigation-dependent relief.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year, with the division flagged Do Not Travel; state hate-crime law omits gender identity; advocacy advisories warn travellers.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; the state human-relations commission enforces employment protections; no documented police sweeps or extortion of trans people.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Violence sits at an elevated version of background risk rather than an organised campaign; recourse for bias assault at state level is thin.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The sole facility prosecution was dismissed on standing, leaving the statute untested and operative; travel advisories from 2023 are unresolved as to current status; litigation on marker and care rules is pending.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil-liberties litigation, legal-aid guidance and injunctions exist, but none has produced a durable traveller-facing remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved appellate status means the traveller meets the restriction as enforced today, with remedy uncertain and slow.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has a birth-sex rule across all public buildings with courts rejecting complaints, polite streets, inclusive private hotels and no trans offence. This jurisdiction is similar on the facility rule but worse overall: a criminal-trespass mechanism with a documented arrest and men's-ward holding, documented abusive immigration custody, entry-stage refusal and lifetime-ineligibility risk, and care restrictions — so it sits below 0.35-A.

0.45-A is a birth-sex bathroom rule in all publicly funded buildings upheld by courts, with ordinary emergency care and private hotels inclusive. This jurisdiction matches the universal facility exclusion but adds entry-document refusal, detention abuse and care squeeze, so it is materially below 0.45-A.

0.25-D combines a universal birth-sex facility rule and ward placement with routine rejection of complaints plus recurrent police stops and extortion threats. This jurisdiction lacks documented police extortion or raids, so it sits above 0.25-D, but its entry-detention and custody abuse narrow the gap.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a stack of state-imposed universal exposures rather than organised street targeting. A visitor who needs a restroom in an airport, courthouse, park or campus meets a birth-sex facility rule enforced by on-site officials and criminal trespass; a passport whose marker or appearance invites doubt meets a national screening posture that can refuse the case, detain, and consider lifetime fraud ineligibility; and the detention that follows is documented as abusive, with conversion-style prison policies and reported sexual violence in immigration custody. Care access is contracted by coverage bans, physician-only rules and conscience refusals. Protections — private businesses outside the statute, a national gender-identity hate-crime statute, injunctions on care provisions, local ordinances — are real but do not reach the border, the facility or the cell. The one prosecution collapsed on standing, so the facility rule remains untested and operating. Remedies exist but are slow and unresolved, placing this materially below acceptance-with-working-remedy tiers and below the single-axis 0.35 anchors, though above tiers of active police or militia targeting.
